# Apply Fixes

## Change Summary

No additional fixes were applied in this Apply Fixes stage. The latest review approved the round-10 budget-tracking amendments without follow-up changes, so the code remains as produced in the most recent implement stage.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Reviewed the latest validation output and confirmed the round-10 review approved the implementation with no required amendments.
2. [Completed] Verified that no additional code or documentation edits were necessary for the residual clamp assertions, `SiphonDetritus` budget coverage, or source-water carbonate fallback validation changes.
3. [Skipped] Rerun validation after applying fixes.

## Validation Evidence

- Review outcome was `approved` with no follow-up amendments or blocking findings.
- No new validation commands were run in this stage because no code changed.
- The latest review recorded `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passing.
- The latest review recorded `cargo test -p tank_core --test budget_tracking --test chemistry --test water_change_mass_balance` passing, including the new `SiphonDetritus` export and carbonate fallback rejection regressions.
- The latest review recorded `cargo test -p tank_data` passing, plus `cargo test -p tank_core` across the full `tank_core` suite and `cargo clippy -p tank_core -p tank_data -- -D warnings` passing.

## Outstanding Risks

- The canonical helper coverage guard for element-bearing state remains convention-based rather than reflective; future explicit N/C pools with non-standard names will require updating the discovery rules and tests together.
- Complex multi-process stages such as `system:nitrogen_cycle` still rely on snapshot-derived gross component budgets, so same-component turnover inside a single stage can remain collapsed until those systems emit fully explicit source/sink deltas.
- The carbonate validation path only special-cases the known non-finite neutral fallback outcome; if future solver changes introduce different internal failure modes, the validation helper will need to be extended in lockstep.
